chapter: Move to New York and the Stuyvesant
title: Kindler's book and Bunk falling asleep to Jelly Roll records
summary: They wonder what became of Kindler's book; Russell recalls Kindler playing Library of Congress Jelly Roll records for Bunk, who fell asleep.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Remembering Jelly Roll Morton: the man, the band

blocks.x: By the way, what ever happened to Kindler in the book he was writing? You know anything about it?
I don't know anything about it. I think he finished it, and it was supposed to have been pretty good, but I don't know about the publication.

I never did know what happened to him. I know one funny thing that happened one day, he wanted to get Bunks' reaction to Jelly Rolls' Library of Congress records. He'd gotten a few of them that Lomax or somebody had given him tests, which Lomax really wasn't supposed to give out. I gave some later to Charles Smith and I, too, and then Spivak, the head of the department, found out about it and stopped it right in the middle of the series, or after we had about two-thirds. But anyway, one day he brought those up to play for Bunks. He wanted to get his reactions and see what Bunks had to say about Jelly. He was going to write it up in his book or something, I guess, in the chapter on Jelly Roll or something. So he got Bunks sitting down and stuff in Gene's apartment. And before the first number was over, Bunks was sound asleep. He never heard of nobody, never got one word out of Bunks. That's all he was interested in hearing Jelly. Go ahead. You're talking about him. Every time I think of him, I think of that little Bunks story. It's frustrating. Yeah.
